name: Date input
summary: Use Date input to collect a memorable or document-based date as separate day, month and year fields.
whenToUse: Use for dates users know or can copy from a document, such as date of birth or passport issue date.
Use an example hint in the order expected by the service.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for dates users need to choose from a calendar, such as an appointment slot.
Do not use a single unstructured field when the service needs day, month and year separately.
Do not use input type=number because its interaction and formatting are unsuitable for date parts.

anatomy.name: Fieldset and legend
anatomy.description: The date question groups its parts and references the example hint.

anatomy.name: Date-input group
anatomy.description: A uniquely identified govuk-date-input contains the ordered parts.

anatomy.name: Day, month and year inputs
anatomy.description: Each part has its own label, text input, numeric input mode, width and submitted name.

variants.name: Day, month and year
variants.use: A complete date in UK service order.

variants.name: Error
variants.use: Highlight only the invalid parts where possible and provide one specific group error.

behaviour: The component requires no GOV.UK JavaScript.
Parse and validate the three submitted strings on the server, including incomplete, impossible and context-invalid dates.
Retain entered values and mark only affected parts when redisplaying an error.
accessibility: Use the fieldset, legend, role=group and unique labels shown in official markup.
Reference the group hint and error from the fieldset and preserve visible focus on each part.
Use inputmode=numeric while keeping type=text so users can enter leading zeroes and avoid number-input controls.
content: Ask which date is required in the legend.
Use a realistic example such as “For example, 31 3 1980” without punctuation that suggests a different format.
Write errors for missing parts, invalid dates and dates outside the allowed context.

htmlExamples.name: Date of birth
htmlExamples.html:
What is your date of birth?
For example, 31 3 1980
